The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

  • Buy AirPods Pro 3 $179 (Reg. $249)
  • Buy AirPods Max $419 (Reg. $549)
  • Buy AirPods 5 from $129

AirPods 5

AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:

Feature AirPods 5 AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case Design Open-ear Open-ear Chip H2 H2 Active Noise Cancellation Yes Yes Transparency mode Yes Yes Adaptive Audio Yes Yes Conversation Awareness Yes Yes Personalized Spatial Audio Yes Yes Live Translation Yes Yes Siri AI Yes Yes On-stem volume control No Yes Charging USB-C USB-C, Qi wireless, Apple Watch Find My case speaker No Yes Battery life (ANC on) Up to 4 hours Up to 5 hours Total battery life (ANC on) Up to 20 hours Up to 22 hours Dust and water resistance IP57 IP57 Price $129 $149

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

If you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice …

AirPods Pro 3

AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

Feature Detail Active Noise Cancellation Up to 3x stronger than AirPods 5 Transparency mode Lets you hear your surroundings without removing your AirPods Adaptive Audio Automatically blends ANC and Transparency mode based on your environment Conversation Awareness Lowers media volume when you start speaking Heart rate sensor Tracks heart rate and calories burned during workouts Hearing health Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features Live Translation Real-time conversation translation via iPhone Fit / Ear tips Redesigned fit with five sizes of foam-infused silicone tips Audio architecture Multiport acoustic design for improved bass and clarity Durability IP57 dust, sweat, and water resistance Battery life Up to 8 hours with ANC enabled; 24 hours with charging case

I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

If you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $179. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

AirPods Max

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

This year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

Feature Detail Design Premium over-ear design with aluminum ear cups and memory foam cushions Chip H2 chip in each ear cup Active Noise Cancellation Up to 1.5x more effective than first-generation AirPods Max Transparency mode Lets you hear your surroundings without removing your headphones Adaptive Audio Automatically blends ANC and Transparency mode based on your environment Conversation Awareness Lowers media volume when you start speaking Personalized Spatial Audio Immersive audio with dynamic head tracking Audio quality Apple-designed dynamic driver and high dynamic range amplifier Lossless audio 24-bit, 48 kHz lossless audio via USB-C Live Translation Real-time conversation translation via iPhone Voice Isolation Reduces background noise during calls Controls Digital Crown for volume and playback; dedicated listening mode button Battery life Up to 20 hours with ANC enabled Charging USB-C; Smart Case preserves battery in ultra-low-power mode

AirPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

If you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

Wrap up
